champion_challenger.fair_comparison_rule: every challenger is compared with the bureau-score policy at its approval count; the as-is policy reads the claimed FICO, which in this generator equals the true score, so it is a reference only

labels.as_is_policy_reference: As-is policy (claimed FICO): sees the true score; not a fair benchmark
labels.challenger_a_xgb_alone: Challenger A: credit_pd_xgb alone, lowest PD up to the champion's count
labels.challenger_b_overlay: Challenger B: the policy with a credit_pd_xgb overlay

overlay_tuning.criterion: lowest total expected loss on the calibration books; ties to the smaller f; infeasible fractions excluded

rule.added: the 500 champion reviews with the lowest credit_pd_xgb PD, excluding fraud referrals
rule.dropped: the 500 champion approvals with the highest credit_pd_xgb PD

drift.auc_test: both books bootstrapped independently (1,000 resamples each); the 95% percentile interval of (book AUC − test-book AUC); the AUC has decayed only if that whole interval is below 0

lower_fico.setting: credit.score_base.mean 755 → 725 (true FICO; claimed and bureau scores move with it)

weaker_dealers.setting: dealerEffect.strength 1 → 2 (dealer quality drives default twice as hard; no applicant feature changes)

drift.calibration_test: observed defaults against Σ model PD, two-sided z-test at 95% with variance Σ p(1 − p)
drift.decay_rule: performance has decayed when the calibration test fails or the AUC test fires
drift.expected_loss_error: Σ model PD × LGD × EAD over Σ true 30+ DPD probability × LGD × EAD, minus 1, on the funded loans (the same default event on both sides, so LGD cancels)
drift.fico_only_method: the book's mean shift in bureau FICO (funded loans) added to every reference funded loan, all other features unchanged, scored by the same model: the score PSI and mean log-odds change from FICO alone
drift.population: each book's funded loans, scored by the headline credit_pd_xgb
drift.psi_method: the existing psi(): ten quantile bins of the reference, a 1e-6 floor on empty bins

air_reference_line.note: 0.80 is the four-fifths screening heuristic from the EEOC's 1978 Uniform Guidelines on employee selection. It is a common informal screen, not a lending legal standard, and crossing it is not a finding of discrimination.

flips.note: audit: flip_sensitive changes the audit record only; deep: the attribute in every layer that holds it, nothing recomputed; financial: region moved with its housing cost (rent multiplier), so DTI follows. Compared: credit decision and reason codes, underwriting decision and codes, every fraud rule, and the credit model's 14 features (identical features give an identical PD and identical reasons).

fairness.interval_methods: approval rate: Wilson 95%; adverse impact ratio: Katz log-scale 95%

as_is_policy_reference.label: as-is policy (claimed FICO): sees the true score; not a fair benchmark

bureau_score_policy.label: bureau-score policy (the champion): the credit policy's thresholds on the bureau FICO

credit_pd_xgb_cutoff.label: credit_pd_xgb: the lowest-PD applications up to the champion's approval count

proxy.method: depth-2 XGBoost (100 trees) predicting the attribute from the 14 features; 5-fold cross-validated AUC, one-vs-rest macro-averaged for more than two groups; percentile interval from 200 bootstrap resamples; top three features by gain named above 0.6

label: Developer testing on synthetic data; the credit policy makes the decision.

reject_inference.fico_effect_definition: mean change in log-odds for +1 SD of bureau FICO (training funded SD), over the seed-42 pool, with predictions clipped to 1e-9 and 1 − 1e-9

challenger_a_xgb_alone.label: Challenger A: credit_pd_xgb alone, lowest PD up to the champion's count

challenger_b_overlay.label: Challenger B: the policy with a credit_pd_xgb overlay

sandbox_candidates.encoding: base64 of numpy.packbits over the pool order (most significant bit first); 1 = approve
